title: Your Shares Just Got a New Way to Change Hands: Understanding Offer for Sale (OFS)
description: An Offer for Sale (OFS) is a way for existing large shareholders, like company promoters or the government, to sell their shares in a company that is *already.

faq.q: What is the minimum public shareholding norm?
faq.a: SEBI requires all listed companies (with some exceptions for PSUs) to have at least 25% of their shares held by the public (non-promoters). OFS is a common way for promoters to reduce their stake to meet this rule.

faq.q: Can anyone apply for an OFS?
faq.a: Yes, any individual investor with a demat and trading account can apply for an OFS through their broker. There are specific reservations for retail investors.

faq.q: Is there a discount for retail investors in OFS?
faq.a: Sometimes, yes. In certain OFS issues, especially those by Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs), retail investors may be offered a discount on the floor price or cut-off price.

faq.q: How do I know about upcoming OFS opportunities?
faq.a: Companies are required to announce OFS details to the stock exchanges (NSE and BSE) at least two banking days before the offer opens. You can track these announcements through financial news, brokerage platforms, or the websites of the stock exchanges.
